title: Implement and export email address validation
acceptance_criterion: The package public interface exports validateEmail, which returns true for user@example.com and first.last+tag@example.co.uk; returns false without throwing for malformed, non-string, empty, whitespace-only, space-containing, and leading- or trailing-whitespace inputs; and npm test passes with regression coverage for these cases.
deterministic_validity_check: node -e "const { validateEmail } = require('./src/index.js'); const accepted = ['user@example.com','first.last+tag@example.co.uk']; const rejected = ['userexample.com','@example.com','user@','user@example','user @example.com',' user@example.com','user@example.com ', '', '   ', null, undefined, 42, {}, []]; if (typeof validateEmail !== 'function' || !accepted.every((value) => validateEmail(value) === true) || !rejected.every((value) => validateEmail(value) === false)) process.exit(1);"
patch_requirements: Create a focused validateEmail utility that returns a boolean for every supplied value and performs no network or external-service calls.
Reject non-string, empty, whitespace-only, leading- or trailing-whitespace, missing-local-part, missing-domain, missing-@, space-containing, and incomplete-domain values.
Accept practical ordinary addresses including plus-addressing, dotted local parts, subdomains, and multi-label domains.
Export validateEmail through src/index.js without changing the existing formatDate public behavior.
Add tests covering all ratified accepted and rejected example categories, including non-string inputs and the no-throw behavior.
